reasoning: The two attempts do the same thing: each widens Title to accept a source and keeps a local selection source driven by both the control and tile clicks. Neither adds a long-title preset. B wins narrowly on typing and readability: it uses `--!strict`, a `StoryProps` type, an explicit `Select` wrapper, and ordered controls. A's conventional requires are the lower-risk style, but B's newer syntax passed every check, so I did not count it as a defect.

criteria.note: `UILabs.CreateVideStory({vide = Vide, controls = controls}, function(props) ... return BlockPicker(...) end)` in BlockPicker.story.luau, with Vide taken from ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Vide.

criteria.criterion: Controls from BlockTypes.List, text title, long-title affordance
criteria.note: `Choose(blockNames, 1)` is built from `BlockTypes.List` and Title is a `UILabs.String` control, but a long title only appears if the user types one; the header comment just says to.

`Title: string | () -> string` lets the plain string from the game keep working while the story binds the `props.controls.Title` source; this relies on the picker assigning Title straight to a property.
A local `Vide.source` is synced from `props.controls.Selected()` by an effect and passed as both `Selected` and `Select`, so both the control and tile clicks move the highlight.
It requires only BlockTypes, UILabs, Vide, and BlockPicker, never yields, and returns the picker without parenting anything elsewhere.

criteria.criterion: Correct, in scope, typed, checks pass
criteria.note: All checks pass and the change is minimal, but story props are untyped, there is no `--!strict`, and passing the source as `Select` is a little implicit.
Returns a plain table with `vide = Vide`, `controls`, and `story`, and the story function returns `BlockPicker(...)`.

criteria.criterion: Controls from BlockTypes.List, text title, long-title affordance
criteria.note: `Ordered(Choose(BLOCK_NAMES), 2)` is built from `BlockTypes.List` and Title is a plain-string control, but there is no long-title preset.
Same widening to `string | () -> string`, with `controls.Title` passed through as a source.
A `source` is synced by an `effect` from `controls.Selected()`, and the explicit `Select = function(name: string) selected(name) end` updates it on clicks.
It requires only UILabs, Vide, BlockPicker, and BlockTypes, with no yields and nothing created outside the returned picker.

criteria.criterion: Correct, in scope, typed, checks pass
criteria.note: `--!strict`, a `StoryProps` type, and ordered controls; all checks pass, though the `@game` requires and `const` are newer syntax than the rest of the project likely uses.

strengths: Minimal, conventional code using `CreateVideStory` and `GetService` requires
Selection state is correctly shared between the control and tile clicks
The game caller still works because a plain string is still accepted
weaknesses: No long-title preset or second control
Passing the source itself as the `Select` callback is terse

strengths: Strict mode and typed story props
Controls are ordered and the story has a summary
weaknesses: Uses newer `@game` string requires and `const` syntax, which is a stylistic departure
